title: introduce-compact-auth-orchestrator-and-multi-sdk-stream-ergonomics
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds a compact auth orchestrator shared interface across TS/Py/Go SDKs; standardizes pull-stream ergonomics; bumps TS SDK to v1.8.0, Py SDK to v0.3.2 and Go SDK to v1.5.1. Backwards compatible; minor migration notes included.
description: Motivation: multiple SDKs had divergent credential-warmup and stream-consumer ergonomics which leaked complexity into application code. This PR introduces a compact auth orchestrator interface and runtime shim that 1) centralizes credential warmup/prefetch logic, 2) exposes a minimal async pull-stream ergonomic facade across TypeScript/ Python/ Go and 3) ships a set of opinionated retry presets tuned for low-latency streaming use-cases. The change is intended to reduce duplicate logic in application-level code and improve parity across SDKs. Summary of changes: -- Introduce compact auth orchestrator (ts): src/auth/orchestrator.ts, with a light-weight in-memory cache, lease hints, and prefetch hooks for token providers. The orchestrator exposes a small surface used by streaming connectors and session facades. -- Add pullstream ergonomic facade (ts): src/stream/pullstream.ts and public exports in lib/index.ts. This provides a simpler async iterator consumer with built-in backoff and checkpoint hints. -- Cross-SDK compatibility: added step-by-step shim examples in examples/multiproto-auth/ demonstrating TypeScript -> Python -> Go usage patterns and fixture scripts used in CI. -- Retry presets: packages/config/retries.ts and docs/retry-presets.md document 'low-latency', 'throughput', and 'conservative' presets used by the runtime. -- Version bumps: package.json updated to 1.8.0; docs updated. -- Tests: added unit tests for orchestrator, integration tests for streaming recovery scenarios, and CI harness changes to run cross-sdk smoke tests in the monorepo pipeline. Migration notes: existing consumer code that called internal credential helpers should switch to new orchestrator.getLeaseHint() or use the facade helper from lib/pullstream; however default behaviour preserves legacy token-provider calls so most apps will not require immediate changes. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-4321) [x] unit + integration tests [x] examples updated [x] docs + changelog entry [x] version bumps for TS/Go/Py (packaging handled in separate release PR). How tested: local unit + integration suite, nightly cross-sdk pipeline, manual verification with a sample chat app using long-running streaming sessions. CI: flakey e2e in first run (timeout in cross-language smoke) was addressed by increasing the test harness timeout and adding a small token prewarm step in the CI job. Performance: no measurable regression on small-scale benchmarks; small latency improvement observed in streaming reconnect paths due to prefetch. Rollout: merged to main and released in the next SDK patch cycle.
